title: Mohd. Akhtar Khan v. State of U.P. and Others
coram: Manoj Kumar Gupta, J.; Prashant Kumar, J.
disposition: Writ dismissed for want of prosecution; 27.5.2011 conditional stay of recovery on a Clause 4.37 footing
headnote: On 27 May 2011 a Division Bench found prima facie substance in the consumer's contention that a purported permanent disconnection dated 8 April 2005, if not made by the competent authority, had to be treated as a temporary disconnection, so that only the outstanding bill as of that date plus six months' minimum charges under Clause 4.37 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 could be charged. The licensee had submitted that permanent disconnection could not have been made as alleged in 2005 because no officer below Sub-Divisional Officer rank was authorised to direct it in December 2010; inspection found the lines unconnected but the meter still installed; the meter was then removed and bills were raised on its readings with minimum charges. As an interim measure the Court stayed recovery under the fresh demand if the petitioner paid the 8.4.2005 arrears plus six months' minimum charges with interest within one month, and called for a counter affidavit. On 21 March 2023 none appeared for the petitioner even in the revised call and the writ was dismissed for want of prosecution, without a final determination of the disconnection or the demand.
facts: Mohd. Akhtar Khan filed Writ-C No. 19028 of 2011 against the State of U.P. and others, challenging a fresh electricity demand after an alleged permanent disconnection dated 8 April 2005. After listings for instructions, the licensee's counsel submitted on 27 May 2011 that permanent disconnection could not have been made as alleged in 2005, because no officer below Sub-Divisional Officer rank was authorised to direct it in December 2010; inspection found the lines unconnected but the meter still installed, after which the meter was removed and bills were raised on its readings with minimum charges. The petitioner contended that a disconnection not ordered by the competent authority had to be treated as temporary, so only the outstanding as of 8.4.2005 plus six months' minimum charges under Clause 4.37 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 were recoverable. On 21 March 2023 none appeared for the petitioner even in the revised call, and the writ was dismissed for want of prosecution.

holding_units.clause: 4.37(a) (minimum-charge billing after temporary disconnection; permanent disconnection after six months if the cause is not removed)
holding_units.topic: Purported permanent disconnection not by the competent authority treated as temporary; only outstanding as of that date plus six months' minimum charges; writ later dismissed for want of prosecution
holding_units.question: Where a purported permanent disconnection is not made by the competent authority, is it to be treated as a temporary disconnection so that only the outstanding as of that date plus six months' minimum charges under Clause 4.37 may be recovered?
holding_units.holding: Prima facie, and only as an interim measure, yes. The Court found substance in the contention that a permanent disconnection dated 8.4.2005 not made by the competent authority had to be treated as a temporary disconnection, so that the outstanding bill as of that date and six months' minimum charges under Clause 4.37 could be charged. Recovery under the fresh demand was stayed if the petitioner paid those sums with interest within one month; a revised provisional bill was then to be issued within 15 days, and default in payment would vacate the stay. The writ was later dismissed for want of prosecution on 21.3.2023 without a merits determination.
holding_units.qualifier: Prima facie and interlocutory (27.5.2011, Sunil Ambwani, J. and Kashi Nath Pandey, J.); the petition was dismissed for want of prosecution on 21.3.2023.
holding_units.flag: Unnumbered order-sheet of six successive listings. Paras 1-4 are listings (1.4.2011, 11.4.2011, 18.4.2011, 13.5.2011). Para 5 is the 27.5.2011 interlocutory order quoting Clause 4.37(a)-(b). Para 6 is the 21.3.2023 dismissal for want of prosecution. Annexure 4.9 in the quoted clause is a notice format, not Clause 4.9. Clause 4.37(b) / s.138 of the Electricity Act, 2003 was quoted and not applied.

holding_units.topic: Writ dismissed for want of prosecution when none appeared even in the revised call
holding_units.holding: On 21.3.2023 none appeared for the petitioner even in the revised call, and the writ petition was dismissed for want of prosecution, without a final ruling on the Clause 4.37 demand.
holding_units.flag: The 21.3.2023 order does not expressly discharge the 27.5.2011 stay; that stay was already self-vacating on failure to pay within one month.

principle_tags.application: Prima facie, a purported permanent disconnection not made by the competent authority is treated as a temporary disconnection, so that only the outstanding as of that date plus six months' minimum charges under Clause 4.37 may be charged; the point was not finally decided.

Recovery under the fresh demand was stayed if the petitioner paid the 8.4.2005 arrears plus six months' minimum charges with interest within one month, on a prima facie Clause 4.37 view, pending a counter affidavit.
None appearing for the petitioner even in the revised call, the writ was dismissed for want of prosecution on 21.3.2023; the Clause 4.37 demand was left unadjudicated.

not_decided.point: Whether the 8.4.2005 disconnection was a valid permanent disconnection by a competent authority, or only a temporary disconnection
not_decided.note: The 27.5.2011 view was expressly prima facie; dismissal for want of prosecution left the character of the disconnection unadjudicated.

not_decided.point: Lawfulness and quantum of the fresh demand beyond the outstanding as of 8.4.2005 plus six months' minimum charges
not_decided.note: A revised provisional bill was contemplated only if the petitioner paid within one month; the writ was later dismissed for want of prosecution.

not_decided.point: Whether unauthorised reconnection after temporary disconnection attracted s.138 of the Electricity Act, 2003
not_decided.note: Clause 4.37(b) was quoted with the clause and not applied.
